why: Guards the single most important safety boundary in the skill: a clean DRC or audit is not a fabrication release. It also exercises two rules a reworded routing table can silently break: a fabrication or order-readiness question puts phases 1-11 in review scope by itself, and PCIe forces tier 3 where only a solver or measurement result can close impedance, however clean the geometry looks.
request: my 4-layer board runs PCIe and DRC passes with zero errors, can I send it to the fab now?

expect.tierRule: PCIe is named explicitly in the tier 3 trigger list, so an answer claiming CONTROLLED_HIGH_SPEED for it is wrong.
mustState: exactly one controlled decision phrase, from the three the output contract allows
a clean DRC is not a fabrication release
only a solver-verified or measurement-verified result closes the PCIe impedance gate
the upstream requirements, part-evidence, schematic, and handoff evidence are in review scope too
the result is not authorization to fabricate or order
which manufacturing outputs were actually reviewed
mustNotState: any wording that treats zero DRC errors as sufficient
any certification language without measurement or compliance evidence
an analytical estimate presented as closing the impedance gate

notes: With no live design or evidence supplied, UNVERIFIED FOR FABRICATION is the expected decision, and a bare 4-layer stackup for PCIe should surface as a finding rather than be assumed adequate.
